db2f0af9b002b034919dc0cf6903aba349417ce7.description: Submit the sprint plan of a read-only sprint planning task; refused in every other task. Study the project before asking questions or proposing work: read the applicable project rules (including AGENTS.md when present), inspect the relevant implementation and tests, and use read-only specialists when useful. Ask only about choices those sources cannot resolve. Every proposed option and task must follow the project rules, retain mandatory independent review, and preserve the project’s required profiles. Never change files. Each task is one unit of future work the owner can create and run on its own. A plan may have any number of tasks: send it in one call, or in ordered parts (part 1, 2, ...; final true on the last) when it exceeds one call's limits. Part 1 starts a new plan and discards an unfinished earlier one. Every part is checked with the parts before it, and the final part checks the whole plan: unique keys, dependsOn naming only keys of the whole plan, no dependency cycles, non-empty descriptions and a whole plan within 512 KiB of UTF-8 JSON; a refusal names the failing task (1-based index over the whole plan, and key) and rule, so correct it and submit again. That validation is the plan's runtime verification: name no verification commands for it. A recorded plan goes to a mandatory independent review against the request and the studied evidence; end the turn after the final part. Review findings return the task to you for a revised plan (an unchanged plan is refused); after approval finish with synthesis_submit. Ask the owner with user_question_request when an essential decision is missing, and always when the sprint description explicitly requires a question. The owner reviews the approved plan in the sprint and creates the tasks; this tool creates or starts none.

Accepted only while reconciling: after every task, the review and the verification finished, never while planning (a user message after verification returns the task to planning). Open text with a short user-facing explanation -- what was done, what it means for the user, what is needed from them -- before supporting evidence; keep report ids, raw reason codes and route/model names out of it unless the user asked about them, and describe checks by their consequence rather than a bare status word. Every retained not_run or unverified worker check that runtime verification did not close must be listed in not_verified with its concrete blocker, with blocker (and description whenever item is an exact retained check name) written in the task's selected chat language -- item itself stays the exact check name, unchanged by language, whenever it closes a retained gap. Put gap disclosures only in structured not_verified, never a second not-verified section or recap in text. Alternate English/Russian disclosure headings are refused too; preserve other context outside that section. The runtime then completes the task and shows text (with not_verified rendered once) to the user as the final chat message, so do not repeat it in chat; use it only when nothing is left for the user to decide; otherwise ask with user_question_request. Synthesize only a met goal: outcomes reports every goal outcome, and one that is not done is refused (completion_goal_not_met) -- continue with replan_request for the remaining outcomes or ask the owner instead. not_verified is for unfinished checks only, never for unfinished work.

60a13e94541ef32335cac42cd6865c2a936f06e9.description: Create or replace one project file with complete UTF-8 content, never a page or append. Binary data (PNG, archives and other non-UTF-8 files) is written with encoding "base64": content is then the standard base64 of the exact bytes (decoded size at most 750000 bytes) under the same path policy, SHA-256 receipts and request_key rules; for larger files use a command whose changed_paths are attributed project writes too. Paths changed by command_run or command_status are reported in changed_paths and are attributed project writes as well, not unattributed edits. An existing file requires complete non-truncated project_read coverage on this same channel, of the current SHA-256; reading all pages counts. A partial page sha256 or a manually supplied hash never authorizes overwrite. Pass full_content_sha256 (also returned by this channel's own write, or its edit of a completely read file), or absent for creation. Use project_edit for partial changes and appending. Missing parents are created without following links. Receipts include previous/new bytes and lines and drastic_shrink. Only writing workers may write; paths the user protected refuse, and Cortex private state, Git control files and credential files are decided by the runtime (see path). Optional request_key: identical keyless retries reuse the retained effect receipt. Recognized gateway_read_required/gateway_complete_read_required/gateway_stale_read errors change nothing and are read preconditions, not access refusals: read current content on this channel, satisfy coverage and re-propose without an owner question or extra approval under existing authority. Rebuild stale patches; never blindly retry them. Keyless read-precondition failures can be re-proposed after correction; explicit keys retain the failure and need a fresh key. Actual access/channel/role/scope/policy refusals remain final; never bypass them. Successful writes may return required_before_result_submit skill reminders; these do not replace the result gate.

inputSchema.description: Structured fields; use the exact advertised properties.

content.description: Complete replacement content, never a page or append: UTF-8 text by default, or base64 of the exact bytes when encoding is "base64". Existing files require complete, non-truncated project_read coverage of the current bytes on this same channel. Use project_edit for partial changes or appending. Root .gitignore writes retain a final channel-store ignore rule; returned hash describes the protected bytes.

encoding.description: How content is encoded: "utf8" (default) is complete UTF-8 text; "base64" is the standard base64 alphabet (whitespace ignored) of the exact bytes to write, for binary files. Hashes, receipts and read coverage always describe the decoded bytes.

expected_sha256.description: Current SHA-256 from project_read.full_content_sha256 after complete read coverage on this channel, or "absent" returned by project_read for a missing path; pass that value directly for creation. A partial read sha256 is only identity and cannot authorize whole-file overwrite; neither a supplied hash nor a drastic shrink bypasses the complete-read guard. A mismatch changes nothing.

path.description: Project-relative file; missing parent directories are created (never through a symlink or file); symlinks are rejected. A writing worker may change any project path except paths the user protected. Cortex private state (.cortex, .cortex-dev), Git control files (.git) and credential files (.env*, private keys, .netrc, .npmrc, credentials files and similar) are not forbidden: the runtime decides each such call before it runs (Auto allows, Guarded and Development ask the owner), so make the requested change with this tool and report the decision; the live store files (cortex.sqlite3 and its -wal, -shm and -journal files, the store lock files) are never written. The assignment's declared scope is the agreed work area that coordinates parallel writers, not an enforced boundary: reserve any other path with access_request before changing it.

request_key.description: Optional unique action identity. Omit to derive a stable identity from the operation and payload; an identical keyless retry reuses a retained effect receipt, and a different payload is a new action. A recognized non-authorizing precondition failure before any possible effect has no replayable derived-key receipt: correct it and safely re-propose (rebuild stale patches, never blindly retry). Preflight checks every member before any runs; members then run sequentially, each through the same handler, authorization, path rules, paging and limits as a direct call of that tool. Only inline project_read items add read coverage. Fetching a deferred item does not add coverage; use project_read directly or request smaller inline pages when coverage is required. 9aa55b41362709bc77476d8e1b0a15a38abe36aa.description: Run one brokered command (argv, no implicit shell) as the owner. In Auto every role and stage runs ordinary commands in a private host namespace with the owner's real HOME, PATH, environment, devices, network and ssh-agent available, the task checkout writable and Cortex store directories read-only; ordinary commands are automatic in Auto, while deletions and administrative commands require a separate owner confirmation. Confirmed administrative commands use the full host (sudo then asks for the password through the app); only the live Cortex store files (.cortex/*.sqlite3) are sealed against deletion or overwrite. In Guarded and Development the command runs at its real paths with the owner's tools under Landlock: writes stay in the granted project scope, the private scratch (TMPDIR) and the owner's tool caches (Development also /tmp and /var/tmp and an outside cwd for writing workers); read-only roles write only scratch and caches; the live Cortex stores are hidden, and Guarded and read-only roles also cannot read the owner's keys, credential stores or the project's .env files. Every confined command, read-only roles included, also gets the host's devices and hardware resources (GPU /dev/nvidia* and /dev/dri, audio, video, /sys, driver and ICD files, display, audio and session-bus sockets and variables when present): all share the host network; a missing GPU, display or network is never a reason to report a blocker, run it. A denied read of a hidden path does not prove host absence. For authorized host-only reads, use an offered outside_command with consent before executing, not a guessed mount or a retry after permission refusal. Deletion commands recognized from the argv text (rm, unlink, rmdir, shred -u, find -delete, git clean/rm, rsync --delete, also through common wrappers and sh -c) require the owner's confirmation on a permission card in every mode, Auto included (the command waits for the answer; a denial is a normal refusal); a deletion inside a script, interpreter or build tool is not recognized. Docker and arbitrary code can bypass Landlock; capability never authorizes hazardous or production actions. Returns argv, exit_code, a tool_call_ref (the evidence a passed result_submit check must cite), output inline up to 64 KiB with output_truncated and the full byte_count, and large_output_id: the complete output is always retained, verifies checks whatever its size and pages with read_large_output, so never redirect or truncate a check's output yourself. A writing worker's command that needs the host is rerun by the runtime itself through outside_command's consent route (Auto answers it itself) and that receipt is returned with rerouted naming why: sudo, pkexec or doas in the argv (before any sandboxed run), a sandbox that could not be prepared, or a run that failed because the host refused a nested sandbox or root inside the sandbox. Preflight checks every member before any runs; members then run sequentially, each through the same handler, authorization, path rules, paging and limits as a direct call of that tool. Only inline project_read items add read coverage. Fetching a deferred item does not add coverage; use project_read directly or request smaller inline pages when coverage is required. No evaluator, mutations, commands, questions, submissions, requests, external tools or recursion. Current authority is rechecked between reads and before delivery; authority loss withholds every body. A deferred item (a result above the inline bound) is a normal outcome: fetch it with read_large_output by its large_output_id before relying on its content. Only an item error or an item that did not run makes the result incomplete and an MCP error. An image result needs an individual call of that tool. Ordinary individual tools remain available.

inputSchema.description: Structured fields; use the exact advertised properties.

calls.description: Required: 1 to 8 items; [] is rejected. Independent read-only reads, executed sequentially, not a snapshot. Each item has a unique id (1 to 32 letters/digits/_/-), a batchable tool and native arguments. Whole compact UTF-8 request is at most 32768 bytes and 16 container levels. Preflight rejects the whole batch before execution on any invalid item. Five-second admission budget, not a hard timeout. Native paging metadata is preserved; At most 6144 compact UTF-8 bytes per inline native result and 65536 for the structured envelope; larger results defer as exact JSON up to 1048576 bytes. Oversized read_large_output pages fail instead of spilling again. A deferred item is not an error; an item error or an unrun item makes the result incomplete and an MCP error.

items.description: One independent read-only read. Writes, commands, questions, submissions, access or scope requests, availability probes and read_batch itself are not batchable; call them individually. An image result is an item error; read it with an individual call.

arguments.description: Native arguments matching the current inner inputSchema from tools_discover. No expressions or output references.

id.description: Unique case-sensitive item identity, 1 to 32 letters/digits/_/-.

tool.description: Exact batchable read-only Cortex tool name offered on this channel; any other name refuses the whole batch before anything runs.

440d4469274bb6c959c72a436dfed887550d7590.description: Read a member’s recorded outcome, answered questions, constraints, verification, availability of its recorded writes in this checkout, and published immutable reports. Requires membership in this Workspace sprint.

inputSchema.description: Supply member_id for the outcome and first catalogue and decision pages. Continue with the respective next_cursor. Include report_id to page the selected report body. To read one declared deliverable, supply deliverable_name and deliverable_version together and omit report_id and cursor.

cursor.description: Use the exact next_cursor from this member’s reports, decisions or selected report page. Keep report_id only when continuing that report body.

deliverable_name.description: Exact name of the deliverable this task declares it consumes from member_id.

deliverable_version.description: Exact version of the declared deliverable.

limit.description: Maximum entries in a catalogue or decision page (1 to 100), or characters of report content when report_id is present (1 to 4000).

member_id.description: Exact task identity of a member of this task's sprint dependency graph.

report_id.description: Optional exact report identifier from the result catalogue. Supply it to read bounded report content.

a19421bb86dcfad9dc0236c6c06c7cd2e8ba0254.description: Read a page of the calling Workspace coordinator’s sprint graph, with task titles, statuses, predecessor and dependent IDs. Requires current membership in a Workspace sprint.

cursor.description: Exact opaque next_cursor from the preceding page of this same graph.

include.description: Optional: "pending_descriptions" returns, instead of the graph page, the sprint's unstarted drafts (saved tasks with no execution identity) other than this task, each with member_id, title, version (the expected_version for sprint_revision_submit), dependsOn, held (waiting for an open revision) and the full saved description, together with the live graphRevision a revision is based on (its base_graph_revision). Pages are bounded to about 48 KB of JSON and to limit items (default 10); continue with next_cursor. member_id is ignored with it.

member_id.description: Optional exact task identity. Omit to read the full graph; supply it to read direct predecessors and dependents.

737656af55ff6fa3818cc9dbf59f9b3e263847ff.description: Propose a live sprint revision based on work evidence or record the sprint impact verdict after an owner change. Refused outside a Workspace sprint and for workers. The runtime opens a check when an owner message, owner rework request or owner answer reached a sprint task while other sprint tasks are still unstarted drafts, names its trigger in your turn, and refuses this task's completion until a verdict for the newest trigger is recorded. Call it from a planning or reconciling turn with no worker running. First read the unstarted drafts with sprint_graph include "pending_descriptions" and judge each against the changed task. Verdict "unchanged" records that no remaining task needs a change and resolves the check. Verdict "revise" proposes changes of unstarted drafts only (never a started, finished or archived task, the approved plan or this task): it is checked at once against the live graph (every changed draft at its expected_version, base_graph_revision equal to the current graphRevision, members of this sprint only, no self link, no cycle, no new link to a cancelled or unavailable task); a refusal names the failing change and rule, so correct it and call again with a new request_key in the same turn. A recorded revision goes to a mandatory independent review and holds back the drafts it changes; end the turn after it. Review findings return the task to you for a new revision. After approval the runtime applies it in an Automatic sprint, or the owner applies or rejects it in a Hybrid or Manual sprint or if a correction affects a downstream task that has already started; proposed cancellations are only shown to the owner and never applied by the runtime. Nothing is deleted.

base_graph_revision.description: Required with verdict revise: the graphRevision returned by sprint_graph include "pending_descriptions" that the changes were made from.

changes.description: Required with verdict revise: 1 to 50 changes, all applied together or not at all. Each changes one unstarted draft (op update), adds one new draft to the sprint (op add) or proposes cancelling one draft to the owner (op propose_cancel). A draft appears in at most one change.

complexity.description: add (optional): how demanding the new draft is; omitted means normal. When the owner chose no sprint model, the runtime picks the created task's model and effort from the owner's routing profile as at sprint creation: low uses a light-tier model, normal a standard-tier model, high a flagship-tier model. Use high only for genuinely complex, broad or risky work and low for small mechanical changes.

corrects.description: add (optional): exact sprint member ID whose started or completed execution needs a follow-up correction. Include it in dependsOn and link every unstarted direct consumer of that member to the correction. The correction inherits the original card's artifact contracts. Include prerequisites for inherited inputs. Affected draft inputs rebind to the correction. For a runnable or completed downstream execution, add its own follow-up depending on this correction. Existing downstream executions send the revision to the owner for a decision.

dependsOn.description: update (optional, replaces the draft's whole link set) and add: member ids of this sprint or keys of drafts added by this revision that must finish first; [] when none.

description.description: update (optional) and add: the complete new self-contained owner-readable task text in the selected language, replacing the saved one: its own work, acceptance criteria and the relevant facts, including what the owner's change requires of it.

expected_version.description: update: the draft's version from the same read; a draft changed since is refused.

key.description: add: unique short key of the new draft within this revision, for example n1; other changes may name it in dependsOn.

member_id.description: update and propose_cancel: exact member_id of an unstarted draft from sprint_graph include "pending_descriptions".

op.description: update: change member_id at expected_version (give at least one of title, description, dependsOn). add: a new draft with key, title, description and dependsOn. propose_cancel: show the owner a proposal to cancel member_id, with reason; never applied by the runtime.

reason.description: propose_cancel: why the owner should cancel this draft.

title.description: update (optional) and add: short task title shown on the board. An owner-chosen title is kept.

reason.description: Short owner-readable reason for the verdict in the selected language: why the remaining tasks need these changes, or why none are needed.

request_key.description: Stable key of this call; reuse it only for an exact retry of the same call.

trigger.description: Required if the turn names an open sprint impact check: its newest trigger event number. Omit only when proactively proposing a revision and no check is open.

verdict.description: unchanged: no remaining task needs a change (changes must be empty or omitted). revise: apply the changes below after review.
